correctness.rationale: For a fully occupied simple ring with exactly b blue and r red (1<=b<=r, n>=3), symmetric p(1/3)=p(2/3)>p(1)=0 makes strict mutual improvement possible exactly when both colors have segregated triple centers. Thus stability requires one color with all runs of length <=2. Alternating run compositions and n/k marked-origin counting give N=F(b,r)+F(r,b)-H(b,r), correctly accounting for labeled ring vertices. Each run contributes min(length,2) integrated vertices, giving maximum min(n,3b) and minimum stable b+min(r,ceil(b/2)+1). Independently enumerated 2,209 labeled profiles for 29 population splits, checked all unlike swaps, total 1,612 stable cases, count and both welfare extrema.
